speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the exact location of your back pain and which part of your leg the pain radiates to? Also, are you experiencing any numbness or tingling sensations in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any weakness in your leg, such as difficulty lifting your foot or standing on your toes? Also, have you noticed any changes in bladder or bowel control, or numbness in the saddle area?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall lifting a heavy weight or performing a specific movement, such as a deadlift, when the pain started? I need to rule out a disc herniation, so please also tell me if you have any numbness or tingling in your foot or toes.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. No prior episodes of similar pain. Social history: Non-smoker, rarely drinks alcohol. Regular gym-goer.

speaker: Doctor
text: To assess for potential nerve root compression, I need to know if you have any specific weakness, such as difficulty lifting your foot (foot drop) or standing on your toes. Additionally, are you experiencing any numbness or tingling in specific toes or areas of your foot?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, changes in bowel or bladder function.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the sudden onset during exercise and radiation down the leg, I suspect a lumbar disc herniation. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Lumbar_Spine.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Evidence of L5-S1 disc herniation impinging on the adjacent nerve root.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI confirms an L5-S1 disc herniation compressing the nerve root, which explains your radiating pain. DIAGNOSIS READY: Lumbar Disc Herniation
